Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Finsolve

Thanks again for taking time today, Sam - great conversation.

Recap of what we covered (TL;DR):
- Pain points:
  - Inconsistent latency under peak loads (50-200 qps spikes) impacting user SLAs.
  - Current on-prem solution has unpredictable preemption and frequent OOMs during long-context inference.
  - Strict data isolation and audit requirements for PHI-related requests.
- Current stack:
  - Model: mix of open Llama variants + a few proprietary scoring models.
  - Serving: in-house TF2/TF-Serving cluster + a small GPU pool for experimental workloads.
  - Peak traffic: baseline ~150 qps, peaks up to ~450 qps for short bursts. Average sequence length ~420 tokens.
- Success criteria for an initial Dedicated engagement:
  - 99th percentile token latency < 300ms for standard prompts at baseline load.
  - Predictable throughput at committed TPS (we discussed 200 TPS sustained, with 2x burst capability).
  - VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs retention for 12 months.
- Capacity & autoscaling notes we discussed:
  - Preferred reserved capacity model: dedicated GPU pool sized for 200 TPS sustained.
  - Burst policy: allow 2x burst for up to 10 minutes with graceful queueing/fallback to cheaper model variant after 10m.
  - Autoscaling: vertical scaling not possible on short notice, so we'll need an autoscaling policy that schedules scale-ups with a 5-15 minute warmup window and a fallback routing rule to lower-cost models when capacity is exhausted.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I'll share a rough capacity estimate and an initial pricing range (attached: capacity_estimate.xlsx).
2) Schedule technical deep-dive with your SRE + our infra team to validate traffic patterns and KV-cache opportunities (suggest Wed 4/22 or Thu 4/23).
3) Legal/procurement to review a tailored SOW & security addendum - I'll loop in Rafael to coordinate.

Notes for the technical deep-dive:
- Please have recent perf/p95/p99 traces and a sample request distribution (we discussed >40% of requests are >350 tokens).
- Confirm maintenance windows and any blackout periods for autoscaling.

Attachments: capacity_estimate.xlsx (stub), redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (stub).

If anything above is off, please flag - otherwise I'll proceed with the estimate and send calendar invites.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa - solid write-up, appreciate the level of detail. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic numbers: baseline is closer to 120 qps for inference calls (I had fuzzed the avg earlier) but we do get daily spikes to ~400 qps for 6-12 minute windows during batch processing.
- Latency targets: p95 < 200ms would be ideal for customer-facing APIs; p99 < 350ms is tolerable.
- Isolation: we need a physically isolated pool for PHI workloads (no bursting into shared pools). Non-PHI workloads can use mixed pools or lower-cost variants.
- Autoscaling: warm-up of 10 minutes is realistic; we would like the option to pre-warm before expected peak windows (we can provide scheduling hints).
- Legal: Priya will need the security addendum and a note on data retention + access patterns.

We can do the technical deep-dive on Thu 4/23 10:00am PT. For that call Amit (SRE) will share perf traces and a short runbook.

Also: can you include any benchmark numbers you have for 8-bit quantized Llama-2 style models on the Dedicated offering? That would help our capacity estimate.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform, Finsolve
